clips.end_words: He knew exactly what he wanted
clips.caption:
Ask someone their name and they answer instantly. Ask them what they want, and most people go quiet.

That silence is the whole problem. Not the economy, not bad luck — just the absence of a specific, measurable thing to aim at. Andrew Carnegie didn't want to be "successful." He wanted to be the largest steel producer in the world, and he could say it without blinking, in any interview, at any time.

You can't hit a target you've never actually named. "More money" isn't a target. A number is.

clips.end_words: to give you what you want
clips.caption:
Everyone says they'll believe it when they see it. That's backwards, and it's the reason most people never see it.

You have to believe it first, while there's still no evidence at all — the same thing an old text calls faith: the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen. Look at a ten-million-dollar mansion while you're broke and think, I'm going to live in this. Someone asks how. You don't know how. You just know.

The moment that belief is steady, the universe starts handing you the how — people, circumstances, timing you couldn't have planned.
